title: The Whales' Turning Place

plate.narration: Above a grassy island, cloud whales turn through the mist. Their long fins move slowly in the open sky. Below them, a broad green landing waits between the clouds.

goal.text: Help the keeper get the whales' island ready before the folds open.

steps.label: Teach the new keeper the signals

whales.narration: Cloud whales sweep their long fins through the mist above a grassy island. Two folds pulse together. Each pulse sends the whales circling back. A kitsune keeper lifts a rope to stop the waiting travelers. "Help me ready the island before those folds open. We need a clear lane and a signal everyone understands." A whale's enormous eye passes overhead. The keeper smooths her whiskers. "They have been watching us make a mess of this all morning."

olivia.narration: Lady Olivia, the unicorn Riftseeker you met on the glacier, waits with a notebook. "Those openings answer each other. I want to open them now." The keeper shakes her head. "The whales are using this space." Olivia points to the rope. "Help me hold the note and I can wake the pair early. It will scatter them. Or guide them clear first. Your choice."

choices.label: Prepare a safe approach before deciding

sky_map.narration: The keeper unfolds a cloth map. Yesterday's lane runs straight into today's sky. "A rock marker, a waiting rope and a broad grass lane," she says. "We set them all out before anyone approaches the folds." Share the keeper's clues to lay out the approach. Olivia holds a corner before the wind can improve the map again.

route_layout.narration: The keeper spreads yesterday's map on the grass. Its whale lane points straight into empty sky. Together you put the waiting rope inland and leave the broad grass lane clear. Olivia erases yesterday's route. The smallest whale rolls overhead, watching the eraser.

whale_listen.narration: A smaller whale with a notched fin vanishes into moving banks of mist. The keeper points out where it went. "Follow that one. We need to know whether it comes around to our lane." Watch the marked mist bank as the banks trade places.

follow_whale.narration: Keep track of the notched-fin whale behind the moving mist banks. You are watching from behind the rope.

interaction.cue: Follow the marked mist bank, then choose where the whale is hidden.

onSuccess.narration: The notched fin comes out where you pointed. Now you can watch that whale through a whole turn.

onFailure.narration: The whale comes out on the other side. You keep your place behind the rope instead of following a guess.

onAssisted.narration: The notched fin comes out where you pointed. Now you can watch that whale through a whole turn.

keeper_points.narration: The keeper points to the notch as the fin clears the mist. "There. Same whale, new view." You watch it together until it faces the lane. Its eye is almost as large as Olivia's notebook.

song_watch.narration: The whale folds one fin, faces the lane, then leaves a quiet pause. The keeper raises her paw in that pause. "That is when it listens." Its next note rumbles through the grass beneath your feet. Olivia stops writing until the sound has passed.

keeper_lesson.narration: The keeper can teach a quiet note or a slow arm signal. The note lets you time an invitation when a whale faces the lane. The arm signal lets your friends hold a visible greeting while another keeper watches its response. "Both leave the whale free to turn away," says the keeper. Which greeting will you practice?

choices.label: Let our songkeeper lead the note

note_practice.narration: The keeper raises a paw for the whale's listening pause. Offer one soft note in that pause, then let the answer come. "Hello," she says. "Not a request for breakfast."

interaction.cue: Offer the note while the marker is in the listening pause.

onSuccess.narration: A soft answering breath rolls back from the mist.

onFailure.narration: Your note overlaps the whale's. You stop and let the keeper show a slower greeting.

onAssisted.narration: A soft answering breath rolls back from the mist.

songkeeper_practice.narration: The keeper raises a paw for the whale's listening pause. Offer one soft note in that pause, then let the answer come. "Hello," she says. "Not a request for breakfast." Your songkeeper can carry the note across a wider part of the pause.

interaction.cue: Offer the note while the marker is in the listening pause.

onSuccess.narration: A soft answering breath rolls back from the mist.

onFailure.narration: Your note overlaps the whale's. You stop and let the keeper show a slower greeting.

onAssisted.narration: A soft answering breath rolls back from the mist.

arm_practice.narration: Hold the keeper's low, open-arm greeting while your acting friend watches the whale. Solo heroes can rest the signal arm on the padded post.

interaction.cue: Keep the greeting steady while the keeper watches.

onSuccess.narration: The whale turns one eye toward the steady greeting.

onFailure.narration: The whale turns one eye toward the steady greeting.

onAssisted.narration: The whale turns one eye toward the steady greeting.

slow_greeting.narration: The keeper offers the greeting herself, leaving a long quiet pause. The whale answers. You listen beside her. Olivia lowers her pencil. "I was about to fill that silence." The keeper smiles. "It was already being used."

lesson_result.narration: The whale resumes its circle. "You have a greeting, not a leash," says the keeper. Olivia sketches its fin, then has to move her notebook when a rolled shelter cloth starts sliding past her hoof.

loose_kit.narration: Olivia catches the rolling shelter cloth against her notebook. For a moment she is a unicorn wearing a very practical curtain. The keeper helps peel it away. "One cloth," says the keeper, "and two places that need it."

waiting_place.narration: There is one shelter cloth. Put it behind the rock and the waiting travelers stay out of the wind, but a watcher must pass signals around the blind turn. Put it at the open viewpoint and the watchers see both folds, but the cloth will need bracing in the gusts. Which work will your party prepare for?

choices.label: Keep visitors sheltered; relay signals around the rock
Keep both folds in view; brace the exposed cloth

shelter_setup.narration: Stretch the cloth behind the rock while the keeper checks the waiting rope. Leave the signal path clear around the blind turn.

interaction.cue: Support the cloth while the keeper fastens it.

onSuccess.narration: The visitors have a dry lee. A watcher will need to carry each signal around the rock.

onFailure.narration: The visitors have a dry lee. A watcher will need to carry each signal around the rock.

onAssisted.narration: The visitors have a dry lee. A watcher will need to carry each signal around the rock.

view_setup.narration: The wind pushes at the cloth. Set its two weighted poles evenly before opening the waiting place. Olivia's mane is attempting to join the flags.

interaction.cue: Level the two cloth poles against the wind.

onSuccess.narration: Both folds are visible from the waiting place. The braced poles hold the cloth.

onFailure.narration: Both folds are visible from the waiting place. The braced poles hold the cloth.

onAssisted.narration: Both folds are visible from the waiting place. The braced poles hold the cloth.

site_ready.narration: The keeper checks your waiting place and takes the first watch. A little whale turns toward the open lane, then hesitates as the folds pulse. Its fin stirs the empty grass. "Give it room to finish that turn," the keeper whispers.

variants.text: From the viewpoint, Olivia can see the whole turn.
Behind the rock, the keeper carries the first sighting back to the sheltered travelers.

little_turn.narration: Wait for the fin to point across the clear grass, then offer the keeper's invitation. The whale decides whether to use the space.

interaction.cue: Wait for the fin-facing interval before inviting the turn.

onSuccess.narration: The small whale turns into the space and swings back toward its family.

onFailure.narration: The whale turns away from the overlapping signals. You lower them and leave the lane open.

onAssisted.narration: The small whale turns into the space and swings back toward its family.

quiet_wait.narration: The keeper asks for one quiet circle. Choose how you will help the waiting place stay calm while the whale looks again.

interaction.cue: Make room for a quiet circle.

options.label: Rest your hands
options.reaction: Hands settle. The signals stop overlapping.

options.label: Tuck loose gear behind the rope
options.reaction: The lane stays empty for the whale.

options.label: Watch without calling
options.reaction: The keeper points out the small fin as it returns.

onSuccess.narration: With the calls quiet, the small whale finds the open turning space.

onFailure.narration: With the calls quiet, the small whale finds the open turning space.

onAssisted.narration: With the calls quiet, the small whale finds the open turning space.

small_whale_result.narration: The small whale has room, but the whole group is still circling. The keeper brings warm barley cakes to your chosen waiting place. Olivia watches a crumb take flight, then eats the next one quickly. A new kitsune keeper arrives to take over. "Show me your signals," she says, "before anyone decides about the folds."

choices.label: Rest, then show the new keeper
Rest while watching one more circle

handoff_sky.narration: The new keeper has not seen your work. The first keeper shows the two cloths. "White means watch this approach," she says. "Striped means stop and wait." The newcomer needs to pass a stop signal from the watcher to the waiting travelers. Anyone can rehearse the relay around the rock. With an open viewpoint, you can instead teach her to watch the cloth signals directly. Which handover will you demonstrate?

choices.label: Use our open view to recognize signals directly

signal_relay.narration: Pass the watcher's stop message along the waiting line. The new keeper receives it at the rock and echoes it toward the travelers.

interaction.cue: Catch the stop message and pass it to the next watcher.

onSuccess.narration: The stop message reaches the waiting place without anyone entering the lane.

onFailure.narration: The stop message reaches the waiting place without anyone entering the lane.

onAssisted.narration: The stop message reaches the waiting place without anyone entering the lane.

signal_memory.narration: From your exposed viewpoint, show the new keeper the cloth changes. She must remember the stop and waiting signs when the watcher turns away.

interaction.cue: Watch the cloth pattern, then echo it.

onSuccess.narration: The new keeper recognizes the changing cloths from the open viewpoint.

onFailure.narration: The new keeper mixes up two cloths. You switch to the watcher relay so every stop gets passed aloud.

onAssisted.narration: The new keeper recognizes the changing cloths from the open viewpoint.

keeper_echo.narration: The new keeper repeats the stop signal, then points out the waiting place on your copied route. The first keeper checks it with her. "A whale's turn is an invitation to watch," says the first keeper. "It is never permission for travelers to cross the rope." The keepers take the watch together.

sky_repair.narration: The keepers have their route copy. Olivia keeps the song observations. If your party meets the lookout keepers farther along this route, you can carry a report of what happens to the whales. It is a promise to bring news, not to make the whales return. Will you take that follow-up job?

choices.label: Promise to bring a whale-route report
Leave today's copies here without promising a report

sky_repair_1.narration: You agree to show the copied map when you meet neighbors who use the island routes. You will say whether the whales were guided or scattered once that choice is made. The keeper asks for honest news, not a promise to make the whales return.

sky_repair_2.narration: You explain that your party does not know where its next crossing will lead. The keeper accepts the limit and keeps the route copies here. Olivia keeps her observations. You have helped make today's choice clear without speaking for a future party you cannot know.

opening_decision.narration: The waiting rope is set. The lane is clear. Olivia looks from her notebook to the circling whales. "Waiting is so slow," she sighs. You can finish the gentle invitation and wait for them to move, or hear her offer to wake the folds early. That shortcut would scatter the whales and disrupt the island neighbors' familiar route. Nobody else will choose for your party. What do you decide?

choices.label: Hear the shortcut before deciding at the rift

gentle.narration: The last tail slips beyond the folds. Both openings spread at once and hold steady. The keeper lowers the rope. "Now they can travel without circling us." Olivia closes her notebook. The pair is ready to cross, or you can pause on the island.

offer.narration: Olivia waits beside the rope. Nothing has opened yet. At the rift, Lady Olivia's way will wake the pair early and scatter the whales. You can still choose to guide them clear instead. The keeper leaves the broad lane open.

guide.narration: The keeper waits beside the open lane. Your party can relay her invitation from watcher to watcher. Your practiced greeting also offers another way: time the quiet note yourself, or hold the slow arm signal while she watches the whales. The whales must choose their own turn. How will you help them clear the folds?

guide_relay.narration: The keeper waits for the leading fin to face the lane. Carry her quiet invitation along the watcher line without adding another call.

interaction.cue: Pass the keeper's invitation toward the clear lane.

onSuccess.narration: The leading whale turns. The others follow its sweep into clear sky.

onFailure.narration: The leading whale turns. The others follow its sweep into clear sky.

onAssisted.narration: The leading whale turns. The others follow its sweep into clear sky.

guide_note.narration: Wait for the leading fin to face the open lane. Offer the note in that listening interval, then leave the whale space to answer.

interaction.cue: Offer the note in the fin-facing interval.

onSuccess.narration: The leading whale answers your note and turns. The others follow.

onFailure.narration: The whale turns away from the mistimed note. You stop calling; the keeper will lead the next invitation.

onAssisted.narration: The leading whale answers your note and turns. The others follow.

guide_arms.narration: Hold the low arm greeting where the leading whale can see it. The keeper watches its fin while your friends steady the signal.

interaction.cue: Keep the arm greeting steady until the keeper sees a turn.

onSuccess.narration: The leading fin tilts toward the greeting. The group follows the new curve.

onFailure.narration: The leading fin tilts toward the greeting. The group follows the new curve.

onAssisted.narration: The leading fin tilts toward the greeting. The group follows the new curve.

guide_wait.narration: The keeper leads one last quiet invitation. Help the waiting travelers leave the lane clear while she watches for an answer.

interaction.cue: Give the whales room to answer.

options.label: Keep the waiting line quiet
options.reaction: Only the keeper's low note carries.

options.label: Clear a loose bag from the rope
Point out the leading fin
options.reaction: The keeper waits until it faces the lane.

onSuccess.narration: The keeper's invitation reaches the listening whale. It turns, and its family follows.

onFailure.narration: The keeper's invitation reaches the listening whale. It turns, and its family follows.

onAssisted.narration: The keeper's invitation reaches the listening whale. It turns, and its family follows.

last_tail.narration: The smallest whale takes its own enormous time. At last its tail clears the folds. The keeper lowers her whistle. Olivia has stopped drawing long enough to watch the sky.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
